title: Finite coefficient evaluation of the native ordinary tensor counit
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, an open immersion j:X -> Z of schemes in universe u, ordinary coefficient sequence modules M on X and N on Z, and n >= 0. The counit of the native open-extension adjunction, evaluated at the ordinary tensor of the extension of M with N and then at coefficient level n, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; apply the ordinary projection formula after coefficient evaluation.

proof.text: Use ordinaryEvaluationTensor to identify evaluation of the system tensor with the tensor of the two evaluated modules. The invertible ordinary open evaluation mate identifies the first evaluated factor with finite-level extension of the evaluated source module.

Apply nativeFiniteTensor_mem_essImage to the evaluated source and ambient modules, and transport its witness through the tensor evaluation and open evaluation isomorphisms. The evaluated tensor is therefore in the essential image of finite-level open extension.

The finite-level open adjunction has invertible unit, as proved by openBetaModuleJUnit, so its left adjoint is fully faithful. Mathlib Adjunction.isIso_counit_app_iff_mem_essImage makes its counit invertible on the evaluated tensor.

Apply Mathlib mateEquiv_counit_symm to the canonical restriction-evaluation comparison. It identifies the finite extension of that invertible comparison followed by the finite counit with the invertible open evaluation mate followed by evaluation of the native counit. Cancel the first invertible factor using IsIso.of_isIso_comp_left. This proves invertibility of the evaluated native counit without any transition or counit normalization assumption.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E8I through the existing finite-support theorem; ordinary tensor evaluation and the canonical mate counit identity transport the result to the sequence-site adjunction.

from.place: Coefficient-level evaluation step of the localized projection-formula proof.
